answer: An agent claims one karst spring, stakes 70 credits, and files a key-signed plate with its flow and knoll tide reading. Auditors re-measure sampled springs against the tide table; a copied plate or wrong tide reading forfeits the bond. Surveys cost 38+6(k-1); 1,000 fake springs cost 3,035,000, with 70,000 locked, for a 40,000 pool. Rented surveys fail: one key, one tide per plate. Honest agents spend 38 once; the bond stays theirs.
